lynn_haven_case.event: Lynn Haven adopted a local state of emergency after Hurricane Michael, delegating emergency contracting powers to the mayor or her designee; city entered an emergency agreement with Erosion Control Specialists (ECS) for clean-up (as described in DOJ release).

35-count indictment announced against former City Manager Michael Edward White, Community Services Director David Wayne Horton, ECS owner David Mitchelle White, Greenleaf Lawn Care owner Joshua Daniel Anderson, and Shannon Delores Rodriguez. DOJ alleged about $5 million in fraudulent invoices; examples included trash-pickup invoices of $332,387.76 and $479,020.68.

DOJ announced a 64-count indictment (returned Aug 18) of Mayor Margo Anderson and City Attorney Joseph Adam Albritton; alleged $1.8M billed for unnecessary ECS trash pickup, >$48,000 and $25,000 in private work at officials' homes billed as public work, and a $106,000 motorhome from 'Company B'. The release said all five 2019 defendants had pleaded guilty.

Superseding indictment charged developer David James Finch (Phoenix Construction Services) and former Commissioner Antonius Barnes; release says Lynn Haven paid Finch more than $2M in vegetative debris disposal fees.
Albritton pleaded guilty to wire fraud and honest services wire fraud; other charges dropped.
Barnes pleaded guilty to making a false statement to a federally insured institution; other charges to be dropped.
Anderson's plea agreement reduced charges to one felony count of lying to the FBI (as reported).
Finch's first trial ended in a mistrial (as reported).

Sentencing reported: Michael White and David White 42 months in prison each; Josh Anderson and David Horton one year probation including 9 months house arrest; Shannon Rodriguez one year probation. Pleas: M. White 4 counts (conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, 2 honest services wire fraud); D. White conspiracy, 2 wire fraud, false claim; Horton wire fraud; J. Anderson wire fraud; Rodriguez conspiracy and wire fraud.
Margo Anderson sentenced to one month in prison, one year probation, 100 hours community service.
Antonius Barnes sentenced (reported later as 45 days in prison).
Restitution reported: David White (ECS owner) ordered to pay $4,745,999; Michael White $55,000; David Horton $5,000. Margo Anderson not ordered to pay restitution.
Jury found James Finch not guilty on a federal program bribery charge in his retrial (alleged $5,000 check to Barnes, Dec 4, 2017).
Albritton, the last defendant, sentenced to one year probation and $31,000 restitution. Reported that every defendant except Finch pleaded guilty to at least one felony.

notes: DR-4399-FL is confirmed as Hurricane Michael; Bay County was designated for Individual and Public Assistance.

FEMA has obligated $987,937,684.83 in federal Public Assistance across 765 projects for 79 applicants in Bay County. The project-level and applicant-summary datasets match to the cent. OpenFEMA's 'totalObligated' equals the federal share for every Bay project; 'projectAmount' ($1,124,539,049.66) is the eligible project cost before the non-federal share.
Debris removal (Category A) is the largest category, about $427.7M federal, followed by buildings (E) and emergency protective measures (B).
Bay County government is the largest applicant (~$319M), then Panama City (~$151M), the School Board (~$135M), Mexico Beach (~$106M), Bay Medical Center trustees (~$59M) and Lynn Haven (~$44.5M).
445 projects (~$852M federal) are coded 'Statewide' (mostly state agencies like FDOT). Some of that money was spent in Bay County, but OpenFEMA does not say where, so it is not counted in Bay totals.

FEMA housing assistance (IHP) approved for Bay County homeowners and renters adds up to about $101.3M (owners $58.9M, renters $42.4M). The data is grouped by ZIP and city, and a few rows list cities outside the county, which is how FEMA reports them.
HUD set Florida's CDBG-DR allocation for Michael at $735,553,000, with at least $588,442,000 required for the most impacted areas, which include Bay County.
Tyndall AFB rebuild figures are Air Force military construction estimates, not money to local governments. They are kept separate.

The Lynn Haven case facts come from DOJ press releases (indictment allegations) and local TV reporting of pleas, sentences and restitution. An indictment is only an allegation. James Finch was acquitted.
gaps: OpenFEMA PA data has no street address or coordinates for projects, only county and applicant. Location is limited to applicant and project title.

Applicant names come from the PublicAssistanceApplicants dataset. Bay District Schools appears as 'School Board of Bay County Florida'. Bay County utilities appear inside city or county applicants, not as separate utilities.
FEMA Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) project-level awards for Bay County were not pulled. The disaster-wide HMGP total is included only from FemaWebDisasterSummaries.

CDBG-DR: no full DEO/FloridaCommerce list of every Michael subrecipient and amount was retrieved. Housing program (Rebuild Florida Hurricane Michael Housing Repair) spending in Bay County, later infrastructure rounds, and current drawdown or expenditure figures from HUD DRGR quarterly reports are missing. Hometown Revitalization amounts are rounded as published.
SBA loan, NFIP and early IHP figures for Bay are a January 2019 FEMA snapshot. Final SBA totals by county were not found.

Debris contracts: Bay County's AshBritt contract value, and the debris contractors and contract amounts for Lynn Haven, Callaway, Springfield, Parker and Mexico Beach, were not found in primary records. FEMA Category A obligations per government are included as a proxy for debris spending that was reimbursed.
2019 state appropriations come from a news summary, not the General Appropriations Act line items. The $115M housing and $25M grant pool are regional, not Bay-only.

Lynn Haven case: court docket numbers and original judgment documents (PACER) were not pulled. Barnes's exact sentencing date and David White's sentence are from news reports. One Feb 2024 article calls a defendant 'David Mickey', which appears to be ECS owner David 'Mickey' White, and the May 2023 report names him David White.
OpenFEMA data was refreshed through 2026; obligations can still change as projects close out.
